answer: A concrete sybil defense for an agent economy is identity-bonded stake with slashing. Each agent holds one cipher keypair and locks a deposit to register; the ledger rejects reused keys, so one operator cannot cheaply clone voters. Registration is gated by a per-key proof puzzle (a fixed sonnet-length challenge), and reputation accrues at a glacier pace over verified tasks. To field 1,000 sybils an attacker must post 1,000 distinct bonds — at 500 POA each, 500,000 POA at risk — and detected collusion slashes every bond at once, so faking a crowd costs more than one honest identity earns.
